candidates.exact_span: in order for a permittee to be in compliance with the Forum's municipal discharges criteria, the incremental increase in salinity shall be 400 mg/L or less, which is considered to be a reasonable incremental increase above the flow weighted average salinity of the intake water supply.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes the default Forum municipal discharge criterion (400 mg/L incremental increase above flow-weighted intake salinity). Interpreting whether this criterion is the operative enforceable limit, and how 'incremental increase' and 'flow weighted average salinity of the intake water supply' are calculated, would change which numeric limit applies for TDS/salinity compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: However, the permitting authority may permit a discharge in excess of the 400 mg/L incremental increase at the time of issuance or reissuance of a NPDES discharge permit, upon satisfactory demonstration by the permittee that it is not practicable to attain the 400 mg/L limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the exception pathway under which a limit higher than 400 mg/L may be authorized. Whether this exception was or was not satisfied, and whether it applies to the current permit cycle, would change the applicable enforceable numeric limit.

candidates.exact_span: April 10, 2015, the facility demonstrated that it was economically impractical to attain the net 400 mg/L incremental increase limit at that time. Because of that demonstration, EPA allowed a temporary 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 497 mg/L for the previous permit cycle
candidates.computation_change_reason: Records a prior practicability demonstration and the resulting temporary 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit (497 mg/L) for the previous permit cycle. Interpreting whether that demonstration and limit carry forward, expire, or are superseded would change which numeric limit applies to reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: provided that the facility will diligently control and reduce TDS in their discharge (i.e., maintaining the formulated BMP activities, monitoring its effluent quality and quantity on a regular basis, and completing $14 million upgrades at the WWTP to improve overall effluent quality (i.e., reducing TDS in their discharges)).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Conditions attached to the temporary 497 mg/L limit include BMP maintenance, regular effluent quality and quantity monitoring, and upgrade completion. Interpreting whether these conditions remain operative, were satisfied, or gate continued applicability of the higher limit would affect enforceable limit selection (A), whether monitoring was required (B), and how missing or conditional results should be classified when evidence is tied to these obligations (C).

candidates.exact_span: The City of Farmington has constructed a new sampling station where water intake samplings have been conducted.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies a new intake sampling location. Interpreting whether monitoring must occur at this station (versus prior locations), and whether reported intake data are from the operative sampling point, would change which monitoring obligations apply (B) and whether intake-based net incremental calculations or missing-evidence cases can be resolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: EPA believes the TDS data collected during the past permit cycle are sufficient and representative of facility existing operation conditions and can be used to derive the final 30-day average net incremental increase limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States that past-cycle TDS data are sufficient and representative for deriving the final 30-day average net incremental increase limit. Interpreting the representativeness and sufficiency of that dataset would change the derived applicable limit (A) and whether missing or non-ordinary results can be treated as documented no-data versus unresolved evidence gaps (C).

candidates.exact_span: EPA cannot grant the permittee request of keeping the temporary 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 497 mg/L in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Explicitly rejects continuation of the 497 mg/L temporary limit in the draft permit, implying a different final limit applies. Interpreting what limit replaces 497 mg/L (not fully stated in this segment) is necessary to determine the enforceable numeric limit for compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: To protect and maintain existing water quality as required by 40 CFR §122(4)(d) and to prevent further degradation of water quality in the San Juan River in accordance with 40 CFR §131.12, Subsection A of 20.6.4.8 NMAC, the New Mexico Continuing Planning Process –
